author: Claude
headline: A software sell-off and a jump in UK inflation keep the focus on steadier companies
summary: US shares fell on Tuesday: the S&P 500 dropped 1.0% to sit just below its 200-day average, and the VIX fear gauge jumped 11% to 25.5. Software companies were hit hardest, with Salesforce down 9.5%, Intuit 7.2% and ServiceNow 6.5%, and the FTSE 100 lost 1.8%. This morning US stock futures are rising after Nvidia beat earnings expectations. But UK inflation has climbed to a one-year high of 3.6% on record diesel prices, which could keep interest rates higher for longer. The picks still favour steady consumer staples, healthcare and payments companies.
points: Nvidia beat expectations and lifted US futures, but it is also warning chip buyers about legal risks tied to China AI access. Tech remains the weakest sector.
UK inflation rose to 3.6%, its highest in a year, driven by record diesel prices. That's a squeeze on UK shoppers and a reason the Bank of England may keep rates high.
Gulf tensions are in the headlines after Iran said it targeted US sites in Kuwait. Oil and gold were both down about 2% in early trading.
Target reports results today and Walmart tomorrow: a key read on how US shoppers are coping.
Bitcoin is stuck near $65,000 after a 12% slide, and every major cryptocurrency is still in a downtrend.
